`__SQL_INSTANCE_ID__` has held memory above 85% for ten minutes.

On PostgreSQL this is the alert that precedes the OOM killer, and the usual cause is connection count rather than data volume: every backend costs several megabytes of private memory before any `work_mem`. Check the connection alert first — if both are firing, the pools are the problem, not the tier.

85% rather than 80%: PostgreSQL deliberately uses free memory for its shared buffer cache, so a healthy instance sits high. The threshold is set where it stops being cache and starts being pressure.

Source: reliability-and-disaster-recovery.md section 17; networking.md section 11.
